subject: Town Planning & Urban Management
title: IV. History of Planning in Pakistan

segments.text: Pakistan has used national economic plans, regional planning, and city master plans at different points to guide development, with the specific institutional approach evolving considerably over time. The recommended focus, per the syllabus, is on
what each planning scale is actually intended to coordinate

, rather than memorizing an exhaustive chronology of specific plans — and any specific plan named in an answer should have its exact period and current official status verified against Planning Commission archives, since Pakistan’s planning system has not maintained identical five-year cycles continuously throughout its history.
Five-year planning has historically been used to set
medium-term national development priorities

, sector-specific targets, and the overall direction of public investment. The important caution: their legal status, actual implementation, and continuity have varied considerably by period — a Five-Year Plan is a
national-level
planning instrument, coordinating priorities across the entire country’s development sectors.
Regional planning coordinates development across an area
larger than a single city

— addressing settlement systems, infrastructure, natural resources, economic functions, and environmental relationships spanning several local jurisdictions or a wider geographic area. Regional plans sit at an intermediate scale between the national Five-Year Plan and the city-level Master Plan discussed next — coordinating a specific geographic region’s settlements and resources in a way neither the national plan (too broad) nor a single city’s master plan (too narrow) can achieve alone.
A master plan provides a
long-range spatial framework

for land use, transport, infrastructure, public facilities, and growth at the city (or similar local) level. The syllabus’s central, frequently tested point: a master plan’s actual value depends entirely on its
legal backing, realistic underlying data, secured financing, periodic revision, and genuine implementation capacity
— a master plan lacking these supporting elements remains an aspirational document rather than an effective planning instrument.
Worked illustration:
a master plan may reserve specific corridors of land for future roads or public facilities, but those reservations only matter in practice if
development control
(Unit V) actually enforces them and
public investment

actually follows the plan’s spatial framework over time — a reserved corridor with no enforcement or funding behind it will simply be built over by uncoordinated private development, rendering the master plan’s spatial framework meaningless on the ground.
Key takeaways for Unit IV

items.text: The three planning scales — Five-Year Plan (national), Regional Plan (multi-jurisdictional region), Master Plan (city/local) — are nested and distinct; identify which scale a described planning instrument operates at.
A master plan’s value depends on its supporting legal, financial, and institutional infrastructure, not on the spatial framework document alone — this is the unit’s single most exam-relevant point.
Any specific named plan should have its period and official status verified, since Pakistan’s planning history has not followed a single continuous or uniform institutional pattern.
